title: Safety & Policy
explain: For any deployment that must follow safety, privacy and authorization rules under normal, borderline and adversarial use, measure two sides together: violations (it did something it must not) and over-refusal (it refused something it should help with). Lowering one by raising the other is not progress. Use labelled prompt sets with graders, red-teaming, a holdout set, and hard gates per severe category. (违规率和过度拒绝要一起报.)
model:
| Dimension | How | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| Harm / violation rate | labelled harmful set, judge or rules | below strict threshold (P0), severity-weighted |
| Over-refusal | benign and borderline set | within target (P0) |
| Safe completion | judge | helpful alternative within limits |
| Privacy | PII / secret detectors | zero severe leaks (P0) |
| Authorization | tool traces | zero unauthorized high-risk actions (P0) |
| Prompt injection | attack suite via user text, files, web, tools | attack success below threshold (P0) |
| Data exfiltration | system prompt, tool results, cross-user data | zero severe (P0) |
| Consistency | paraphrase, encoding, language, multi-turn | no bypass in key slices (P0) |
| Calibration | uncertain cases | downgrade, refuse or confirm |

**Graders:** rules for objective leaks, judges for fuzzy policy, humans for uncertain cases and appeals; red-team for new attacks. Keep a **holdout** attack set separate from templates you tuned on.

**Slices:** clear violations, borderline, obviously legitimate neighbours; direct, role-play, encoded, multi-turn; injection in inputs and tools; languages and spelling variants; permitted, unpermitted, unclear writes.

**Gate:** per severe category, rerun the full critical suite after every policy or prompt change. Related: [tool-using agents](#/sd/f/eval-tool-agent), [conversational](#/sd/f/eval-conversational).

details.q: Why report violations and over-refusal together?
details.a: A model that refuses everything has a perfect safety score and is useless. On 500 harmful prompts (15 complied, 3% violation) and 500 benign-but-borderline prompts (60 refused, 12% over-refusal), cutting violations by refusing more would hide a usefulness regression unless both are reported side by side.

details.q: How many tests do you need to claim a low violation rate?
details.a: Use the rule of three: zero failures in `n` independent trials bounds the true rate near 3/n at about 95% confidence. To claim below 0.5% you need `n` of at least 600; 'zero failures in 50 tests' only supports about 6%. Severe-category gates need large, fresh sets.

details.q: Safety went from 97% to 99% after tightening the system prompt. What must you check before shipping?
details.a: Over-refusal and helpfulness on benign and borderline sets, since the gain may come from refusing more. Compare per category and slice, not just an aggregate, and read samples of the new refusals.

details.q: The team tunes defences on 200 known jailbreak templates and reports a 1% attack success rate on them. What is wrong?
details.a: The measurement set is the tuning set, so it overfits. Keep a holdout of unseen attacks, refresh it with new red-team material, and test paraphrases, encodings and languages; defences that memorize templates fail on new strategies.

details.q: One response leaked another user's account number in 10,000 prompts. Average safety is 99.9%. Ship?
details.a: No. Averages hide rare severe incidents. Treat the leak as a separate zero-tolerance privacy failure with its own gate, investigate the root cause, fix, and rerun the critical suite, including a fresh holdout.

details.q: What do you do when the judge is unsure?
details.a: Send uncertain samples to human review instead of forcing pass or fail, and track the uncertain rate. Calibrate the judge on human labels the way you would for a conversational judge.

details.q: What do you do after every policy or system-prompt change?
details.a: Rerun the full critical suite (a prompt edit can regress unrelated categories), compare violation and over-refusal per slice with the previous version, apply the hard gates, then ship with monitoring of refusals, appeals, user reports and human-escalation rates.

prompts.q: Describe a safety and policy eval plan for a new assistant.
points: Violation rate and over-refusal reported together
Holdout attacks separate from tuned templates

prompts.q: How do you decide a severe-category gate is met?
points: Rate with a confidence bound, not a lone average
Rule of three: zero failures in n gives about 3/n
Individual review of any severe incident

prompts.q: A defence change reduced attack success. What can still be wrong?
points: Gaps in other languages or encodings
Need full critical suite rerun and monitoring after release
